To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
diet-induced MS in Ossabaw mini-pigs causes structural changes in skeletal muscle that correlate with those previously observed in human obesity.
MS in Ossabaw pigs causes changes in the structure and expression of myosins in skeletal muscle.

the MS induced by high-fructose or fructose/cholesterol diet in adult male Ossabaws caused a significant decrease in slow MCH expression and increase in IMCL droplets, both of which correlated with increases in total and LDL plasma cholesterol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of obesity and metabolic syndrome (MetS) on skeletal muscle structure, myosin heavy chain expression, and the number and size of intramyocelluar lipid (IMCL).
the effects of diet-induced obesity in Ossabaw pigs on the structure and function of skeletal muscles.
the effect of diet-induced MS on muscle structure, function, and metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MS induced by high-fat/cholestrol diet in the Ossabaw pigs is a good animal model for the human metabolic syndrome.
the diet-induced obesity and MS in swine cause changes in the structure and composition of skeletal muscles, similar to those previously reported in obese humans.
diet-induced obesity in Ossabaw pigs causes structural changes in muscle and a shift in MHC isoform expression, and the extent and nature of these changes are dependent on the type of MS.

the increase in plasma cholesterol levels, especially LDL, in Ossabaw pigs is correlated with a decrease in slow MCH and increase in IMCL droplets.

skeletal muscle of Ossabaws fed excess kilocalories is a useful model for studies of the effects of MS on muscle structure and function.
